title: Cache keys and values, sample a token, search a beam, and verify a draft
brief: Count flops against bytes for decoding, size and build a KV cache, turn scores into a token with temperature, top-k, and top-p, search with a beam, and write the accept-or-replace rule of speculative decoding.
hints: A matrix times a batch of B vectors does 2 * B flops per weight and reads b bytes per weight, so the ratio is 2 * B / b. Decoding one token reads every weight once, so the time is n_params * bytes_per_elt / bandwidth. The ridge point is peak_flops / bandwidth, and you need 2 * B / b >= ridge, so round B up.
kv_cache_bytes is 2 * n_layer * n_kv * d_head * seq_len * bytes_per_elt. The leading 2 is one copy for keys and one for values.
KVCache.append should add one array of shape (n_kv, d_head) to a per-layer list. KVCache.get should np.stack that list on axis 0, and return empty (0, n_kv, d_head) arrays when nothing is stored.
cached_attention_step: scores = K @ q / sqrt(d_head), softmax them (subtract the max first), then return weights @ V. One query against T cached rows gives a (d_head,) vector.
apply_temperature divides the logits by the temperature, subtracts the maximum, exponentiates, and divides by the sum. The subtraction keeps a temperature of 0.001 from overflowing.

For top-k, np.argsort(-probs)[:k] lists the k largest. For top-p, sort descending, take np.cumsum, and keep up to and including the index np.searchsorted(cumulative, p, side='left') returns. Clamp that index to len(probs) - 1. sample_token at temperature 0 returns int(np.argmax(logits)), and otherwise draws with rng.choice(len(probs), p=probs) from the rng you are given.

A draft token x is drawn with probability q(x) and kept with probability min(1, p(x) / q(x)), so the chance that x survives is min(p(x), q(x)). The residual is np.maximum(p - q, 0) divided by its sum, and when p equals q the sum is 0, so return p.
speculative_accept: draw u = rng.uniform(). If u is below min(1, p[x] / q[x]) return x. Otherwise draw a replacement with rng.choice(len(p), p=residual_distribution(p, q)). Use rng for both draws.

beam_search: keep a list of (tokens, raw_score) pairs. For every pair and every token j with a finite log_probs[tokens[-1], j], build an extension, sort all extensions together by -score (a stable sort), and keep the first beam_width. Extensions that end in eos go to a finished list instead of the beam. Rank finished hypotheses by raw / ((5 + L) / 6) ** alpha, where L counts the generated tokens and not bos.
